about: Every instruction, error code and README edge case of the Solana Foundation DvP program at the pinned commit, paraphrased and cited by file and line, mapped to Impulse. An item with no 'pending' field is answered by exactly one test in tests/parity tagged with its id and a verdict (format in tests/parity/parity.rs); 'pending' names the later increment that answers it, and a pending item may have one test tagged partial for the part merged code can express. Each claim traces one row of the spec's head-to-head table: its Solana cell to items, cited source lines, the on-chain measurement in solana-onchain.json, or a note that it is not supported or contradicted; its Impulse cell is copied, with a note where the tests show less. A measured or contradicted trace names the upgrade authority only as {upgrade_authority}, which the generator fills from the decoded on-chain record. scripts/gen-parity.sh joins this file, the test tags and the test results into PARITY.md. Each entry of 'prose' traces one sentence of the spec outside that table in the same ways, or marks it 'none' when it says nothing about the program, and carries a proposal in design-property wording where it is not supported; 'see' names items whose current verdicts are shown beside a trace. An item marked client_side is one whose Solana answer is a check the client runs, so an off-chain Impulse check can answer it as an equivalent. Owner: the parity suite (I10).

source.licence: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Solana Foundation (LICENSE at the pinned commit). Nothing is copied; items are paraphrased and cited, and only identifiers (instruction and error variant names) are reproduced.

deployment.set_by_title: its title says it sets declare_id to the deployed program address

items.summary: Permissionless. Allocates the trade account, its nonce tombstone and both escrow token accounts; moves no funds.
Signed by either party. Returns the signer's own leg in full; the trade stays open and the leg may be funded again.
Signed by the settlement authority only. Moves each leg's agreed amount to its settlement destination in one transaction, refunds any surplus to the depositor and closes the trade and its escrows.
Signed by the settlement authority. Returns every funded leg to its depositor and closes the trade, also after expiry.
Signed by either party. Returns every funded leg to its depositor and closes the trade.
After close only. The depositor supplies the original seeds; the program requires the nonce tombstone and returns a deposit that landed in a recreated escrow.
Reclaim, Reject or Recover signed by someone other than the two parties.
Settle after the expiry time.
Settle or Cancel signed by someone other than the settlement authority.
Settle before the earliest settlement time.
Settle while an escrow holds less than its leg amount.
Create with an expiry at or before the current time.
Create with the earliest settlement time after the expiry.
Create with the same account as seller and buyer.
Create with the same mint on both legs.
Create with a zero amount on either leg.
Create with a Token-2022 mint carrying an amount-changing extension or a non-transferable one.
Create with the settlement authority equal to either party.
Create with an executable settlement authority, which could not be credited the rent of the closed accounts.
Create with seeds and a nonce whose tombstone already exists, so the address served an earlier trade.
Create with an expiry more than one year after creation.
Create with a client reference longer than 64 bytes.
Recover while the trade account is still open; Reclaim is the path while the trade is live.
Recover with seeds whose address has no nonce tombstone, so no trade ever existed there.
Create while a non-native escrow account holds SOL above its rent-exempt minimum; the close paths would sweep that SOL to the closer.
Create with a settlement destination equal to the trade account itself, which would make delivery a self-transfer that succeeds without moving anything.
Create while the trade account holds SOL above its rent reserve; closing would sweep it to the closer.
Any value-moving instruction when a recipient or refund token account's recorded owner or mint no longer matches the expected wallet and mint.
Create with a party that is not a system-owned, non-executable account, for example a token multisig, which could never sign an unwind.
Settle when a leg's mint authority differs from the one recorded at Create.

Each side funds its leg with a plain token transfer to the leg's escrow account, with no program call; mints with transfer hooks or pause need a checked transfer carrying extra accounts, or the deposit fails.
A native SOL leg uses wrapped SOL; the program syncs the wrapped balance before reading it, so raw lamports sent to the escrow count and go back to the depositor.

items.solana: SOL preload of a token escrow
items.summary: Create refuses a non-native escrow preloaded with SOL above rent; SOL sent to such an escrow after creation cannot be prevented and goes to whoever closes the trade.
Anyone holding the mint can add tokens to an escrow, so Settle moves exactly the leg amount and refunds the surplus to the depositor.
Each leg's proceeds go to the counterparty or to a settlement destination fixed at Create; refunds always go to the depositor, and destinations are terms a funder must check.

items.solana: Owner reassignment of a recipient account
items.summary: A legacy SPL token account's owner can be reassigned without changing its address, so every value-moving path re-reads the recipient account's owner and mint.
An optional client reference of up to 64 bytes is stored with the trade; the program never reads it.
Reclaim, Cancel and Reject return the escrow's actual balance, not the leg amount.

items.solana: Late deposits, including a front-run reject
items.summary: A deposit can land after the trade closed, including when a counterparty rejects ahead of an in-flight funding transfer; Recover with the tombstone returns it.
The rent paid at Create goes to whoever closes the trade, so a payer who is not the closer subsidises the closer.
Only Settle stops at expiry; Reclaim, Cancel and Reject always work, and funding transfers are not checked against expiry.
With an earliest settlement time set, Settle also waits for it; without one there is no lower bound.

items.solana: One-year expiry cap and its inheritance
items.summary: The one-year expiry cap bounds how long rent stays locked, and the earliest settlement time inherits it because it may not pass the expiry.
Time gates use cluster time, which lags wall-clock time and can jump; the README advises budgeting about a minute of drift and avoiding boundaries.
Each seeds-and-nonce combination maps to one trade forever through a tombstone that is never closed, so a closed trade's address cannot be reused with new terms.
Parties must be accounts that can sign; a token multisig party is refused, and a custodian routes through a smart wallet instead.
Create is permissionless and the economic terms are not part of the account address, so anyone can create a record with any terms for any parties.

items.solana: Nonce squatting and 64-bit values in clients
items.summary: A predictable nonce lets a third party take the trade's address first; nonces and amounts must stay 64-bit integers in TypeScript, since a JavaScript number above 2^53 rounds.
items.pending: I9: the TypeScript SDK's handling of 64-bit nonces and amounts. Not run by the parity crate: the SDK is reached only through its wasm build or a dependency on impulse-wasm, which would change Cargo.lock outside the parity crate; the SDK's own suite is the check until then.

items.solana: Verification before funding and look-alike records
items.summary: Funders must check the stored terms, the account owner and its exact size with checked helpers before depositing, or a look-alike record can drain the escrow they fund.

Amount-changing extensions are refused at Create and checked again at Settle; permanent delegate, freeze, pause, default frozen state and close-and-recreate are accepted as trusted-authority risks that can stall or move a leg.
Transfer-hook mints need extra accounts resolved off chain, at most 32 per leg; a mutable hook can later block every transfer of the leg.
The program never creates user token accounts; all four recipient accounts must exist before Settle, and dust in an escrow forces a surplus refund, so a missing account reverts settlement.

items.solana: Surplus refund as a second transfer
items.summary: Settle's surplus refund is a second transfer of the same mint reusing the leg's hook accounts; for some hooks it fails and blocks Settle until the depositor reclaims and funds exactly.

The README's deploying note says the declared program ID is a placeholder whose keypair is not available, so the program has not been deployed at it, and that deploying without a fresh keypair and regenerated ID lands at the wrong address. At the pinned commit the note is stale: lib.rs declares another ID, set by a later commit whose title calls it the deployed address (see Source and measurements).
A depositor can withdraw a funded leg at any time before settlement (Reclaim), so funding is always revocable.

claims.capability: Fund with a plain transfer, no program call
claims.impulse_note: A KAS leg is one plain payment. A KCC-20 leg is funded with two outputs, a token owned by the vault's script hash and a KAS authorizer at the vault address, and the token alone cannot move: a token-only deposit waits until a KAS output sits at the vault address (EDGE-01 runs the fund builders and the engine).

claims.capability: Escrow address bound to the terms
claims.solana: No: terms stored in the account, create is permissionless
claims.impulse: Yes: address is the P2SH of the terms
Recompute the address; a mismatch means nothing to fund
claims.impulse_note: EDGE-19 runs impulse-core's verifier; as on Solana, running the check before funding is the funder's, and the parity tests do not run the command line.

claims.solana: Recover instruction plus a permanent tombstone
claims.impulse_note: Under earmarked funding the depositor waits for expiry_daa, and a late deposit holding other than the leg amount only its depositor can send home (IX-5, EDGE-09).

claims.solana: Forces a surplus refund; a missing account reverts settle
claims.impulse: Ignored by settle, refundable; an under-funded authorizer or carrier is topped up by the settler
claims.impulse_note: Holds for a separate dust deposit (EDGE-22). An escrow its depositor over-funds does not settle, and only the depositor can send it home, under earmarked funding from expiry_daa (EDGE-04).
Earmarking blocks only the depositor's own withdrawal; the counterparty and the authority can still send the leg home at once (EDGE-25).
Self-settling settles with no authority in EDGE-11; Direct mode is built and run in the engine by the I5 suite (tests/engine/builders.rs), and no parity test runs it.
Direct mode is run in the engine by the I5 suite (tests/engine/builders.rs), and no parity test runs it.
claims.note: Every trade lives in one program account with two escrow token accounts, one per leg; an absence, read from the README's description of the program.
Both legs are amounts of token mints, the cash leg included; an absence, read from the README's description of the program.
A program for swaps on Solana between two token mints; an absence, read from the README's description of the program.

claims.solana: Cluster time; the README advises budgeting about 60 s of drift
claims.impulse: DAA-score lock time; settle-after-expiry is policy (see red team)
claims.impulse_note: EDGE-11 pins that the contract accepts a settle after expiry_daa; the settle builder's refusal is policy (ERR-01), and the lock-time bounds are exact to one DAA score, effectively one higher (EDGE-14).

claims.solana: Rejected; must route through a smart wallet
claims.impulse: Native P2SH or KCC-20 script owner as a destination (delivery, proceeds, refund); v1 builders fund and pay fees from key-owned UTXOs only
claims.impulse_note: As a destination only: a party is one x-only key whose signature the refund entry checks, so a custodian party holds a single or aggregated key (EDGE-16, ERR-22). The cell should say so.

prose.quote: Where Impulse differs from the Solana program on day one:
prose.note: The lead-in of five items, each traced separately below

prose.quote: There is no stored trade record to forge or tamper with; the funder recomputes each address from the agreed terms before funding
prose.note: The program's funder reads and verifies the stored record (EDGE-19); Impulse has no stored record, and EDGE-19 runs the funder's recomputation of each address, which the funder runs before funding

prose.quote: Solana only offers revocable funding
prose.note: The program's unwinds work at any time (IX-1, IX-3, IX-4); EDGE-25 shows Impulse's earmarking blocks only the depositor's own withdrawal

prose.quote: A self-settling mode lets anyone complete a fully funded trade
prose.note: Settle needs the authority's signature on Solana. On Impulse the self-settling modes settle with no authority (EDGE-11); Direct mode is not run by a parity test

prose.quote: The asset leg can be released against an off-chain RTGS or bank payment
prose.note: Both legs of the pinned program are token amounts, an absence read from the README's description of the program; the Impulse side is the external-cash mode, which a parity test runs only as part of EDGE-11

prose.quote: There is no rent, no recovery instruction, no permanent tombstone, and dust deposited separately does not block settlement
prose.note: The Impulse side holds for dust sent as a separate deposit (EDGE-22); an escrow its depositor over-funds does not settle (EDGE-04)

prose.quote: The Solana program is a minimal settlement primitive
prose.note: README.md:11 calls the program minimal

prose.quote: no messaging, matching, compliance or reporting ([solana-foundation/dvp](https://github.com/solana-foundation/dvp))
prose.note: An absence, read from the README's description of the program

prose.quote: How it works:
prose.none: A lead-in to the list below.

prose.quote: a named settlement authority is the only key that can settle
each side funds an escrow account by plain token transfer
one transaction moves both legs
either party can pull back its own leg at any time, and either party or the authority can abort and refund both
Behaviours that its README discloses, each compared in PARITY.md:
prose.note: The README states each behaviour below as a note, cited in the row

prose.quote: Create is permissionless and the terms are not part of the account address
Anyone can create a record with forged terms or attacker-chosen destinations
Every funder must read and verify the stored terms, owner and account size before depositing
A transfer can land after the trade closed. Recovering it needs a dedicated instruction and a nonce tombstone account that is never closed
Anyone can over-deposit into an escrow, which forces a surplus refund. Settle then reverts unless all four recipient token accounts already exist
It has to defend against several token-model quirks:
legacy token accounts can have their owner reassigned
escrows can be preloaded with SOL
Token-2022 extensions (hooks, fees, freeze, pause, permanent delegate) can stall or tax a leg
Rent paid by the creator goes to whoever closes the trade
Time gates use cluster time, which the README says lags wall-clock time and can jump forward; it advises budgeting about 60 seconds
A funded leg can be withdrawn by its depositor at any time before settlement, so a counterparty cannot rely on it until settlement
There is no off-chain cash leg and no cross-chain leg
prose.note: Absences, read from the README's description of the program

prose.quote: No trade settles without the settlement authority
Solana's program has one mode: escrow with a mandatory authority and both legs on-chain
prose.note: 'One mode' and 'both legs on-chain' are read from the README's description of the program (README.md:11, README.md:15), and no row tests an absence

prose.quote: The verifier recomputes both addresses from the terms, so there is no stored record to check
prose.note: The verifier is the funder's check, run by the funder (EDGE-19)

prose.quote: Solana's program declares 24 error codes
prose.note: The program's 24 error codes are ERR-00 to ERR-23. On Impulse's side the contract returns no code: ERRORS.md lists its refusals by tag ([S1] to [R14]) and the codes belong to the off-chain software
